sentences.text: This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 31-05-2022 at about 7.00 p.m., the Petitioner was rider on Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-Q-5617 on T.Begur Thyamagondlu Road, Hanumanthegowdanapalya Gate,
Thyamagondalu Hobli, Bengaluru District, at that time, the driver of Ashok Leyland mini goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA- 52-A-9769 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle), drove the same with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bike.
Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to Thyamagondlu Primary Health Centre, wherein he has taken first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Care Asia Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and is unable to lead normal life as earlier.
It is claimed that Petitioner has spent Rs.3,00,000/- for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.
At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 32 years, working as a driver and earning a sum of Rs.22,000/- per month.

Due to accidental injuries,
he has lost his earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1- Insured and Respondent No.2-insurer.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsels and filed their separate written statements.

4. The Respondent No.1 has denied all the averments of the petition inter-alia contending that the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, the accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Further, as on the date of accident the offending was insured with the respondent No.2 and same was valid as on the date of accident and driver was having valid DL.
On these grounds, he has prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.

5. The Respondent No.2 has filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the alleged offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
Further, denied the contents of petition averments in toto.
It has contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

It has denied that the the accident was caused due to the negligence of driving of the offending vehicle and contended that the accident has occurred due to negligence of petitioner, as he was riding the motorcycle without DL and helmet in a zigzag manner.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
Further contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, excessive and unreasonable.

For all Pradeep .K.C vs Premesh Chandra on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151122442/
2 these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :

-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was riding in his Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-Q- 5617 on 31-05-2022 about 7.00 p.m. on T.Begur- Thyamagondlu Road, Hanumanthegowdanapalya Gate, Thyamagondlu Hobli, Bengaluru District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Mini Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-A-9769?

2. What compensation Petitioner is entitled?
3. What order ?

7. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case,
two doctors are examined as PW-2 and 3 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.27.
8.
The Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.

9. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:-

The case of the petitioner is that on 31-05-2022 at about 7.00 p.m., the Petitioner was rider on Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-Q-5617 on T.Begur Thyamagondlu Road,
Hanumanthegowdanapalya Gate, Thyamagondalu Hobli, Bengaluru District, at that time, the driver of Ashok Leyland mini goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA- 52-A-9769 drove the same with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bike.
Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
11. In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 9.

To support of his claim, Dr.Sreedhara K.C., Consultant neuro physician and rehabilitation at Deepashri Hospital and neuro rehabilitation centre, was examined as Pw-2 and also examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. Orthopedic surgeon at Sanjaygandhi hospital, Bengaluru as PW-3 and they have produced the documents at Ex.P.22 and 27
The Respondent-insurance company has contended that it was the negligence of the rider of motorcycle in causing the accident.

During the cross examination the PW1, learned counsel for the respondent no 2 has put forth suggestion that Pw1 was speed, he could not control his vehicle and Pradeep .K.C vs Premesh Chandra on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151122442/
3 hit rear portion of the goods vehicle and caused the accident.

sentences.text: He denied the same.
He also denied that false complaint was given against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Except cross-examination and contention in the objections, respondent-insurance company has not produced any evidence to prove the negligence of the rider of motorcycle.
13. There are no materials on record to disprove the Petitioner's evidence and to prove the contention of the Respondent.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
After the investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and the copy of the charge sheet is produced at Ex.
P.9 . FIR registered against the offending vehicle driver, charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

14. ISSUE NO.2 :- As per Ex.P.8 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1) Communited compound fracture of patella.
The doctor opined that the above injury is grievous in nature.
15. Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injury.

Immediately he was taken to Thyamagondlu Primary Health Centre, wherein he has taken first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Care Asia Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as a driver and earning a sum of .22,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
Dr. Sreedhara K.C.

Consultant neuro physician and rehabilitation/ Mental health and MLC consultant at Deepashri Hospital and neuro rehabilitation centre, Bengaluru, has deposed that petitioner has sustained injury to head and H/o LOC + ENT bleed + with GCS E1VTM4, pupils 2mm bilaterally equal and he was treated at Care Asia hospital.

On 02- 07-2024 at Deepashri hospital,
PW-2 has examined the petitioner and he complains of difficulty in walking, poor social interaction,
not able to do prolonged driving and he is able to tell only 4 things.

Further, PW-2 has stated that as per Neuro- psychological assessment report petitioner had mild impairment of motor speed,
focused attention, sustained attention, category of fluency, working memory, response inhibition,
learning verbal memory, verbal comprehension, visuospacial construction. Considering the above

,
Pw-2 has opined that petitioner was unable to work and assessed the whole body disability at 26.6%.

17. PW-3 Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. Orathapedic surgeon at Sanjaygandhi hospital, Bengaluru, has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained communited fracture of left patella in a RTA and he was treated in the form of ORIF with TBW in Care Asia hospital.

He found that the fracture is united Pradeep .K.C vs Premesh Chandra on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151122442/
4 with OA changes and restrictions of movement of right knee.

On examination he has assessed the total permanent physical disability for lower limb at 40% and to the whole body at 13%, which is permanent in nature and petitioner will have difficulties in daily activities.
18. On careful reading of evidence of PW-2 and PW3, makes it clear that they have not treated the Petitioner.
During the course of cross examination they denied that they have falsely assessed disability.
It is pertinent to note that PW2 and PW3 has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.
19. Further the petitioner has stated that he is a driver.
However, he has not produced any documents to substantiate that he surrendered his driving licence as he is unable to drive now due to his permanent disability.

Therefore, considering that the grievous injury is on the leg and considering the difficulties and evidence of PW-2 and PW3 and also by considering the age of the Petitioner, the functional disability is assessed at 11%.
20. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 32 years.

Ex.P.15 - DL shows that he was born on 08-07-1990, the same is considered as age of the petitioner as on the date of accident as 32 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 16.
21.
The age of the petitioner is 32 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.
He was admitted to Care Asia Hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as a driver and was earning Rs.22,000/-P.M.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.

In the absence of material with regard to source of income,
the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
22. The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2022, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 15,500/- Per Month.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
23. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability: Looking into the nature of injuries, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.
As the Petitioner is a driver, considering nature of injury and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 11%.

24. Further the petitioner was aged about 32 years as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 16.
the national income taken as Rs 15,500 x 12 x 16 x 11/100= Rs.3,27,360/- towards loss of future income.
25. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained leg injury and was inpatient for a period of 3 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .30,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.

Pradeep .K.C vs Premesh Chandra on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151122442/
5 26.
Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .25,000/- under loss of amenities of life.
27. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.12 amounting to 44,153/- and Ex.P.16 for Rs.16,503/-.
There is no evidence forthcoming to disbelieve the said medical bills.
More over, the material available on record appears that the respondents have not seriously disputed those documents.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded compensation of .60,656/- towards Medical Expenses.

28. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges: Ex.P.10-Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was admitted at Care Asia Hospital, Nelamangala, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 31-5-2022 to 02-06-2022 i.e., for a period of 3 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .20,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
29. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
considering 3 days admission in the hospital as inpatient and around 3 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 3 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .15,500/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .15,500 x 3 = 46,500/-.
33.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
Sl.N Nature of Compensation Amount o.
1. Loss of future earnings  3,27,360/-
2. Pain and Sufferings  30,000/-
3. Loss of amenities  25,000/-
4.

Medical expenses  60,656/-
5. Conveyance, Food,  20,000/-
Nourishment & Attendant charges 6. Loss of income during laid  46,500/-
 up period

Total  5,09,516/-
Pradeep .K.C vs Premesh Chandra on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151122442/
6
34. Liability: Respondent No.1 being the owner and the Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.
However, Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
35. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner

is awarded compensation of Rs.5,09,516/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized or scheduled bank of his choice for a period of 2 years.
Remaining 75% amount shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
